gloss: how me- changes the first sound
title: me- and its sound changes
pattern: p → mem- (pakai → memakai) · t → men- (tulis → menulis) · k → meng- (kirim → mengirim) · s → meny- (sapu → menyapu)
explanation: me- blends with the first sound of the root, and four sounds disappear into it: p becomes m (pakai → memakai), t becomes n (tulis → menulis), k becomes ng (kirim → mengirim) and s becomes ny (sapu → menyapu). Other first sounds stay, with a matching mem-, men- or meng- in front (membeli, mendengar, mencari, mengambil, mengganti), and before l, m, n, r, w and y it's plain me- (melihat, memasak, merokok). To look a word up, take off the me- part: if a vowel follows mem-, men- or meny-, the root has lost its p, t or s (memakai → pakai, menunggu → tunggu, menyewa → sewa), unless it simply began with m or n (memasak → masak, menikah → nikah). After meng- and a vowel, try k or nothing: mengirim → kirim, mengambil → ambil.
natural: You need this whenever you read: signs, menus, messages and the news are full of me- words, and a dictionary lists them under the root. It also helps with casual speech, where nunggu, ngirim and nyewa are just menunggu, mengirim and menyewa without the me-.
stiff: Keeping the first letter (mempakai, mentunggu, mengkirim, mensewa) is the usual learner's slip, and it's always wrong with everyday words. A few borrowed words do keep it, such as mentraktir (to treat someone, from traktir), but you'll meet those one at a time.

gap.why: The p of pakai drops after me-, leaving memakai.

examples.english: I've been waiting for an hour.

gap.why: The t of tunggu drops after me-, leaving menunggu.

examples.indonesian: Ibu saya mengirim paket dari Bandung.
examples.english: My mum sent a parcel from Bandung.

gap.why: The k of kirim drops after me-, leaving meng- before the vowel: mengirim.

examples.indonesian: Saya mau menyewa motor untuk seminggu.
examples.english: I'd like to hire a scooter for a week.

gap.why: The s of sewa drops after me-, leaving meny-: menyewa.
